sentences.l2: 在短视频盛行的今天，人们的阅读方式正悄然发生着改变。
sentences.l1: In today's world where short videos are prevalent, people's way of reading is quietly changing.

sentences.l2: 通勤的地铁上、睡前的床头，越来越多的人习惯于刷抖音，在几分钟甚至几十秒的画面切换中获取零散的信息。
sentences.l1: On the subway during the commute, at the bedside before sleep, more and more people are used to scrolling Douyin, picking up scattered information through picture switches lasting a few minutes or even a few tens of seconds.

sentences.l2: 这种碎片化阅读固然便捷，却也悄然侵蚀着我们的注意力——习惯了高强度刺激的大脑，往往难以再长时间停留在一段文字上。
sentences.l1: This fragmented reading is indeed convenient, but it also quietly erodes our attention: a brain accustomed to high-intensity stimulation often finds it hard to stay on a piece of text for long.

sentences.l2: 有研究者指出，长期依赖短视频的人，在阅读长篇内容时更容易感到疲倦与焦躁。
sentences.l1: Some researchers point out that people who rely on short videos over the long term more easily feel tired and irritable when reading long content.

sentences.l2: 于是，静下心来读书，反倒成了一件需要刻意坚持的事。
sentences.l1: So, settling down to read has instead become something that requires deliberate persistence.

sentences.l2: 然而，深度阅读所给予的思辨能力与审美体验，是任何速食式内容都无法替代的。
sentences.l1: However, the critical thinking ability and aesthetic experience that deep reading gives are something no fast-food-style content can replace.

sentences.l2: 我们或许不必彻底拒绝短视频，但应当为读书留出一段完整而不被打扰的时光，让思维在字里行间重新沉淀下来。
sentences.l1: We perhaps need not refuse short videos entirely, but we should set aside a complete and undisturbed stretch of time for reading, letting thought settle down anew between the lines.
